desc: Formalize the model: per-cell port variables, A/B allowed port sets, toroidal boundary consistency via shared edge-variables h/v.
Key derivation: all constraints are linear over GF(2); each valid port pattern = exactly one tile orientation, so answer = number of GF(2) solutions = 2^{nullity} or 0.
Reduce to graph parity problem: equations x_u⊕x_v=c form a constraint graph; answer = 2^{#components} if all components consistent, else 0; solve with weighted (parity) DSU.

Implement Python solution: parity DSU with packed arrays (array('i') parent, bytearray potential), index mapping v_{i,j}=i*W+j and h_{i,j}=HW+i*W+j, per-cell equation emission (A: 2 eqs with c=1; B: 3 eqs with c=0,0,1), conflict → 0, else pow(2, components, 998244353).

Verify correctness on the three sample cases (2, 0, 2) via tracing; edge cases checked (H=2/W=2 wrap-around distinctness, all-B 2×2 → 4 matches brute force, DSU find path-compression and union formula proven correct).
Finalize code: fast stdin parsing via read().split() for up to 1e5 test cases / 1e6 total cells, memory ~12MB with compact arrays, output per test case.
